Spectral density operator encapsulates global eigenvalue behavior through integration over eigenvalue space; it maps directly to GSI’s Bayesian updating of ensemble parameters. Eigenvalue correlation kernel provides local structure via orthogonal polynomials, enabling GSE to model transitions between eigenstates by encoding level repulsion. Trace identity relation links matrix traces to eigenvalue moments, forming a bridge between deterministic matrix operations and stochastic spectral inference. These primitives collectively define a hierarchy of observables: from global spectral measure to local correlations to moment-based inference. Their failure modes include breakdown at non-Hermitian limits or when eigenvalue degeneracy dominates. Dualities emerge in the thermodynamic limit where microscopic correlations yield macroscopic universality classes.
